newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn ends lower on harvest, late local sales.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn ends lower on harvest, late local sales.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on harvest pressure and late local selling, traders said.
"There's a lot more corn left to be harvested than beans," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Weekend corn combining was said active and harvest should remain active this week under nearly ideal weather, the traders said.
Corn was firm early on a jump in soybeans and on short-covering tied to a technical correction, better than expected exports and talk that China may be seeking U.S. corn, the traders said.
"The export inspections were pretty good for corn," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
USDA said U.S. corn inspected for export during the week ended October 31 totaled 43.858 million bushels, well above trader expectations for 20 million to 30 million bushels.
Traders were skeptical of the China talk.
"There's still talk China is looking for corn but no tonnages were mentioned," Kucha said.
Corn closed one to 3-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 1-1/4 at $2.61-3/4. March was down 1-3/4 at $2.67-3/4.

Traders said they expected the release this week of corn crop estimates from Farmers Commodities Corp, Sparks Companies and the Leslie-ADM Elevator Survey. USDA in October estimated the corn crop at 9.012 billion bushels. USDA's November report is slated for release November 12.
"The market is talking about a 9.2 billion bushel corn number and 2.4 billion bushel beans," Kucha said.

Traders said the short-term technical indicators continue to show corn is oversold. The nine-day relative strength index (RSI) on a daily basis for the December closed at 12.6 points. The trade views an RSI of 30 or less as indicative of an oversold market. December Friday closed at 13.5 points.
But the longer term moving averages show corn remains in a bearish downtrend, technical traders said.

The first resistance for December was at $2.65-1/4 per bushel and second resistance was at $2.69. First support was at $2.61-1/2 and second support at $2.57-3/4. The session high for December was $2.65-3/4 and the session low was $2.61-1/4.

Iowa Grain and Rosenthal Collins each bought five million bushels of December, Smith Barney sold two million bushels each of March and May while Tenco Inc sold 2.5 million bushels of March, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 60,000 contracts, down from 66,767 Friday.

Corn options players keyed on R.J. O'Brien's purchase of 400 March $3.20 calls at 1-1/8 cents, Goldenberg Hehmeyer bought 500 March $2.50 puts at three cents and Refco Inc sold 300 March $2.80 calls at 6-1/2 to seven cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 24,000 contracts, down from 41,002 Friday.
